editorial:
Imagine a world where you can buy a robot best friend to keep your kids company. That is exactly where you land with this story. You follow Klara, a sweet and curious robot who just wants to be loved. When she gets picked by a girl named Josie, you can tell right away that they are meant to be. Josie is going through a lot of pain and has a rocky relationship with her mom, but Klara's kindness starts to change everything. It feels like a warm hug of a movie, blending futuristic ideas with a lot of heart and some of that quirky humor Taika Waititi is known for.

The acting is top-notch, and the way the robot's perspective is shown makes the world feel fresh and bright. While the story moves a bit slow in the middle, the emotional payoff at the end makes it worth your time. If you enjoy stories about friendship and family, you will love this one.
endingExplained: In the end, you find out that Klara was designed to replace Josie if the girl ever passed away from her illness. However, Klara chooses to be a true friend instead of a copy. As Josie grows up and moves on to a new life, Klara is left behind in a scrap yard. She spends her final days remembering the love they shared, showing that her feelings were real even if she was just a machine.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional stories about friendship and futuristic worlds.
